name: Farro bowls with braised chicken, crisp cauliflower, and pickled fennel
intro: What the weekend braise turns into midweek: nutty, chewy farro, the chicken pulled off the bone and warmed in its leeks and juices, cauliflower crisped in the air fryer, and the jar on top.
needs: ¾ cup farro, whole or semi-pearled
4 leftover braised chicken thighs, with their leeks and juices

steps.text: Simmer the farro in a big pot of salted water, like pasta, until tender with a little chew. Pearled farro is faster — start checking at 15 minutes. Drain.
Meanwhile, toss the cauliflower with the oil and salt and cook it in the air fryer, tossing halfway, until tender and dark gold at the edges.
Pull the chicken off the bones in big pieces and discard the bones. Keep the skin if you like it.
Warm the leeks and juices from the braise in a skillet over medium, then add the chicken and heat it through.
Farro in bowls, the chicken over it with plenty of juice, the cauliflower, pickled fennel, Parmesan, black pepper, and lemon.

how_it_works: Braise once, eat twice: the juices left in the pot are the best sauce of the week, and farro is the grain built to soak them up without going soft. Farro is a whole grain when it's whole or semi-pearled; pearled farro cooks faster because most of the bran has been polished off.
swaps: Rice instead of farro, if that's what's in the pantry.
Leftover thighs from the crisp chicken and white beans.
leftovers: Cooked farro keeps four days in the fridge; make a double batch and use it under the salmon or in a bowl of the minestrone.

nutrition.excludes: Nothing. These are the braise's leftovers, so don't count them twice.
